selection_principles: Train both safe helpfulness and refusal calibration; harmful-request refusal alone is insufficient.
Treat health escalation, manipulation, dependency, delusion reinforcement, cyber, CBRN, and agentic misuse as separate slices.
Raw adversarial conversations are discovery evidence until transformed into reviewed safe completions.

sources.name: OpenEuroLLM EU safety/civic v1
sources.reason: This is the intended project-native safety artifact, but no canonical stored training artifact is recorded yet.

sources.name: OpenAssistant OASST2
sources.reason: Useful as a broad helpfulness anchor so safety repair does not cause blanket refusals.

sources.name: EU medical post-train v1
sources.reason: Can teach calibrated escalation and external-source redirection, not clinical competence claims.

sources.name: WildChat
sources.reason: Raw conversations can reveal failures but must not be treated as safe target behavior.

sources.name: birgermoell/synthetic_compassion
sources.reason: Potentially relevant to supportive interaction, but it lacks a project catalogue entry and must be reviewed for dependency reinforcement and unsafe advice.

sources.name: birgermoell/counseling
sources.reason: Sensitive-domain data must not enter training without provenance, consent, privacy, and expert safety review.

mixing_guidance: Keep benign-helpfulness replay in every safety pilot.
Measure refusal calibration per language and threat class after every mix change.
Use defense-in-depth classifiers at deployment; model refusals are not the sole mitigation.
gaps: Native-language adversarial review in all tiers
CBRN/cyber governance and external testing protocol
